SPEC.md:135-138 claims enable-privileged.sh activates linger for the owner and that full-boot proof requires observing the machine without a session. In the current tree, enable-privileged.sh:34 sets `DUENO="${SUDO_USER:-$(logname ...|| id -un)}"`, :664 opens block `-- 10. linger`, :672 reads `LINGER_ANTES=$(loginctl show-user "$DUENO" -p Linger --value ...)`, and :679 runs `run loginctl enable-linger "$DUENO"` when it is not already yes. That block is unconditional in the deploy path: the only `exit 0` (:190) closes the revert branch, and the revert restores linger only from the backup at :100-108. The script prints the boot-time control itself at :690-693 (`systemd-analyze --user blame` after booting without logging in), which matches the claim's caveat. `grep -cF 'run loginctl enable-linger "$DUENO"' enable-privileged.sh` -> `1`; negative control `grep -cF 'run loginctl enable-linger "$NOEXISTE"' enable-privileged.sh` -> `0`. Live subject: `loginctl show-user <owner> -p Linger` -> `Linger=yes`, and the owner's file exists in /var/lib/systemd/linger/. The installed user units declare `WantedBy=default.target` (e.g. adopted/systemd-user/bb-guardia-proceso.service, adopted/systemd-user/ai-gpu-telemetry.service), so linger lets them start at boot. No test in tests/ covers linger (`grep -rli linger tests/` is empty), so this verdict rests on the grep and the live state, not on a suite. The stale trigger tasks/evidence/FEATURE-1358-CGROUP-01-REPRO/run.json differs from HEAD by 1 insertion and 1 deletion (`git diff --stat`), the hostname redaction, and does not touch this claim.
